items.title: Compact mobile writing, recoverable trash and measured Windows exit
items.author: styayur

files.patch:
@@ -36,6 +36,8 @@ jobs:
         run: |
           pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium --only-shell
           pnpm test:ui
+      - name: Restore survives real writer process termination
+        run: dotnet run --project tools/GitPadPlus.FaultProbe -c Release -- "${{ runner.temp }}/gitpad-restore-faults" artifacts/restore-process-faults.json --restore
       - name: Dependency security
         run: |
           pnpm audit --json > artifacts/npm-audit.json

@@ -50,7 +50,7 @@ Depth strategy: opaque surface steps for functional content. Only transient menu
 
 ## Responsive behavior and accessibility
 
-At <=760px, one-column workspace with calendar navigation toggled by Calendar. Opening a note focuses the writing view; returning to dates is explicit. Header uses two compact rows. Tabs/formatting scroll horizontally, title/actions stay compact, body padding 20px. Layout uses dynamic viewport height and `interactive-widget=resizes-content` with Android AdjustResize. Keyboard-visible viewport retains scrollable editor and reachable toolbar, never hides commands permanently. Do not imitate software keyboard using an image or claim browser emulation as native Android evidence.
+At <=760px, one-column workspace with calendar navigation toggled by Calendar. Opening a note focuses the writing view; returning to dates is explicit. Browsing keeps date navigation, while writing uses one editable-title/action row without the brand header. Tabs/formatting scroll horizontally, title/actions stay compact, body padding 20px. Layout uses dynamic viewport height and `interactive-widget=resizes-content` with Android AdjustResize. Keyboard-visible viewport retains scrollable editor and reachable toolbar, never hides commands permanently. Do not imitate software keyboard using an image or claim browser emulation as native Android evidence.
 
 All controls: hover, pressed, focus-visible, disabled. Focus 2px with offset, visible in high contrast. Dialog semantics, form labels, real buttons/select/details. Calendar arrow keys move by day/week, Home/End within week, PageUp/PageDown month, Enter/Space select. Note selection uses aria-current. Overflow regions remain keyboard scrollable. Loading and errors remain textual/live; no fake status. Honor zoom and 320px widths; preserve usable editor line width at 1366/1920 screens and 100/125/150/200% browser scaling. Native DPI and software keyboard require actual native checks, separately documented from browser coverage.
 
@@ -65,3 +65,25 @@ Android requires the application-level MAUI WindowSoftInputModeAdjust.Resize pol
 ## Review discipline
 
 Methodology: Dammyjay93/interface-design at 2f9be3206855bcb2d1d0af262c8bae25cba6658d; read SKILL.md plus design-review and design-deslop commands. It supplies the review lenses, not a dashboard template. Screenshots must be actual application output. Review focal point, typography/color, surface/depth, composition, states, and reuse independently; record findings and fixes, with untested/native limits explicit. No stock moodboard, decorative artwork or fabricated runtime screenshot is needed for this writing tool.
+
+## Mobile workflow v1.1, in progress
+
+On writing widths up to 760 CSS px, use the existing editable title as the single
+document heading, with Calendar, Settings, Save, Image and More in its action row.
+At 360px and below, Settings and Image move into More. Calendar and Save retain
+44px targets. Browsing provides Back to writing when a document is open.
+
+The existing plugin-owned formatting strip docks to the bottom of the resized
+viewport. A 48px reserved strip keeps the shell status immediately above it.
+Native SafeArea and AdjustResize own keyboard compensation. CSS adds no keyboard
+height or second native inset. Commands target the editor that most recently
+received focus, preserving its instance and selection.
+
+A note row reveals an 88px trash action after a leftward touch of at least 48px.
+The first 24px at the screen edge is reserved for system navigation. Vertical
+intent cancels the gesture. Recycling requires the explicit trash action.
+Keyboard focus reveals the same action. Undo remains available for ten seconds,
+and Settings exposes persistent Trash and Restore. The signed development probe
+has passed actual Android touch reveal, short/vertical gesture protection, Undo
+and persistent Trash restore with equal raw Markdown and sidecar hashes. This
+qualifies the observed development probe, not a final release package.

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+# GitPad+ UI v1.1 closeout
+
+## Implemented
+
+Branch `ui/mobile-workflow-v1.1` starts from main `63070c81c99f90cd4e46a7ce4d700ace2d08b5fa`. The existing alpha tag and public prerelease predate this work. PR [#6](https://github.com/styayur/gitpad-plus/pull/6) isolates the mobile workflow, recoverable trash and exit diagnostics. This report distinguishes development-probe acceptance from release qualification.
+
+Mobile writing keeps the existing editable title and one action row. Calendar, Settings, Save, Image and More share that row; Settings and Image overflow below 361px. Calendar offers Back to writing. The existing plugin-owned command strip docks to the resized viewport with status above it. Native Resize and SafeArea own IME compensation. Formatting follows the last focused editor without rebuilding it. The secondary pane has compact mobile Save/Close controls and status in the footer.
+
+Note rows expose an explicit trash action after 48px leftward touch movement. The action is 88px wide. Vertical intent cancels tracking, and the first 24px screen edge remains available for system navigation. Only one row expands. Keyboard focus offers the same action. A live gesture ref handles pointer move/up delivered within one React render turn; a real native swipe failure exposed the previous rendered-state race. Recycling closes matching tabs/panes and offers ten-second Undo. Settings has persistent Trash and per-note Restore. Dirty, Saving and SaveError states block recycling, and native deletion checks dirty state and revision. Navigation responses predating recycling cannot reopen the deleted note.
+
+Core adds shell RPCs `documents.trash` and `documents.restore` within protocol v1. Plugin capability allowlists are unchanged. Restore copies original source bytes, validates IDs and raw hashes, retains durable restore intent, completes interrupted operations before deletion recovery, and commits by moving the entire transaction folder into a retained restored archive. An exact replay after source commit but before index acknowledgement can rebuild the disposable index and return the original note. Changed active targets remain conflicts.
+
+Windows adds optional `GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE` phase and dispatcher measurements. Tracing is disabled normally and records no document text or credentials. The sampler observes visibility and waits for the OS process handle to signal, records build hashes, UTC/monotonic clock correlation and observer lag, and computes median/nearest-rank P95/maximum. A startup window handle can change, so visibility is armed only after a visible current handle is observed. No shutdown kill, skipped save or fixed-delay workaround was added. No operational exit-latency fix is claimed.
+

 DocumentSession is a per-note single-writer queue. It snapshots edits, sends the previous acknowledged revision/hash, retains a newer buffer during delayed saves and reports errors without dropping content. Native requests are serialized at the WebView boundary. A timeout/cancellation cannot undo a committed native operation; reload before retrying uncertain writes.
 
 Block tracking traverses nested block nodes and persists structural paths in the sidecar. Invertible identity steps participate in actual ProseMirror history so Undo/Redo restores identities without a content-keyed cache; ordinary copies allocate fresh UUIDv7 IDs. Each rendered editor session owns a distinct DOM instance. Two distinct notes can be edited in separate panes; the workspace stores the secondary note ID. Recovery explicitly archives all conflicting inputs and any open editor buffer before applying selected Markdown. Portable/browser and native evidence are recorded separately.
+
+## Local trash restoration
+
+Protocol version 1 adds two shell RPC methods, documents.trash and
+documents.restore. The former returns NoteSummary entries from retained
+tombstones. The latter accepts an id and returns the original Note after
+restoring the exact source pair. Plugin capability grants are unchanged.
+
+Restore rejects an occupied active identity before recording its intent. A
+restoring.json record binds the retained Markdown and sidecar hashes. Restart
+recovery completes that intent before applying old deletion tombstones. After
+both original files validate, the complete tombstone folder moves atomically
+under .gitpad/restored, and the disposable index is rebuilt. The archive
+preserves the previous deletion transaction. Restoring a different source over
+an occupied identity raises a conflict and retains the source copies.

Verify native mobile gestures and restore durability; measure Windows exit
Cover trash RPC conflicts and background workspace recovery
Align acceptance scope and mobile design documentation

 ## Review discipline
 
 Methodology: Dammyjay93/interface-design at 2f9be3206855bcb2d1d0af262c8bae25cba6658d; read SKILL.md plus design-review and design-deslop commands. It supplies the review lenses, not a dashboard template. Screenshots must be actual application output. Review focal point, typography/color, surface/depth, composition, states, and reuse independently; record findings and fixes, with untested/native limits explicit. No stock moodboard, decorative artwork or fabricated runtime screenshot is needed for this writing tool.

+## Mobile workflow v1.1, in progress

+On writing widths up to 760 CSS px, use the existing editable title as the single
+document heading, with Calendar, Settings, Save, Image and More in its action row.
+At 360px and below, Settings and Image move into More. Calendar and Save retain

+
+The existing plugin-owned formatting strip docks to the bottom of the resized
+viewport. A 48px reserved strip keeps the shell status immediately above it.
+Native SafeArea and AdjustResize own keyboard compensation. CSS adds no keyboard

+qualifies the observed development probe, not a final release package.

@@ -0,0 +1,83 @@
+# GitPad+ UI v1.1 closeout
+
+## Implemented
+
+Branch `ui/mobile-workflow-v1.1` starts from main `63070c81c99f90cd4e46a7ce4d700ace2d08b5fa`. The existing alpha tag and public prerelease predate this work. PR [#6](https://github.com/styayur/gitpad-plus/pull/6) isolates the mobile workflow, recoverable trash and exit diagnostics. This report distinguishes development-probe acceptance from release qualification.
+
+Mobile writing keeps the existing editable title and one action row. Calendar, Settings, Save, Image and More share that row; Settings and Image overflow below 361px. Calendar offers Back to writing. The existing plugin-owned command strip docks to the resized viewport with status above it. Native Resize and SafeArea own IME compensation. Formatting follows the last focused editor without rebuilding it. The secondary pane has compact mobile Save/Close controls and status in the footer.
+
+Note rows expose an explicit trash action after 48px leftward touch movement. The action is 88px wide. Vertical intent cancels tracking, and the first 24px screen edge remains available for system navigation. Only one row expands. Keyboard focus offers the same action. A live gesture ref handles pointer move/up delivered within one React render turn; a real native swipe failure exposed the previous rendered-state race. Recycling closes matching tabs/panes and offers ten-second Undo. Settings has persistent Trash and per-note Restore. Dirty, Saving and SaveError states block recycling, and native deletion checks dirty state and revision. Navigation responses predating recycling cannot reopen the deleted note.
+
+Core adds shell RPCs `documents.trash` and `documents.restore` within protocol v1. Plugin capability allowlists are unchanged. Restore copies original source bytes, validates IDs and raw hashes, retains durable restore intent, completes interrupted operations before deletion recovery, and commits by moving the entire transaction folder into a retained restored archive. An exact replay after source commit but before index acknowledgement can rebuild the disposable index and return the original note. Changed active targets remain conflicts.
+
+Windows adds optional `GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE` phase and dispatcher measurements. Tracing is disabled normally and records no document text or credentials. The sampler observes visibility and waits for the OS process handle to signal, records build hashes, UTC/monotonic clock correlation and observer lag, and computes median/nearest-rank P95/maximum. A startup window handle can change, so visibility is armed only after a visible current handle is observed. No shutdown kill, skipped save or fixed-delay workaround was added. No operational exit-latency fix is claimed.
+
+## Automated Tested
+
+- Current local TypeScript, ESLint, 52 Vitest and 23 release/provenance/transport tests passed.
+- Core 51 passed, including exact source pairs and anchors, repeated restore/restart, simulated interrupted stages, conflicting targets, unrelated-note startup, retry after committed restore, and actual RPC rejection of dirty/stale/duplicate deletes with safe restore replay.
+- Four real restore subprocess terminations passed at `RestoreStaged`, `RestoreMarkdownReplaced`, `RestoreSidecarReplaced` and `RestoreCommitted`. Each fixture contains Unicode prose, a block UUID, a selection anchor and a tag. Restart recovered identical Markdown/sidecar bytes and the original indexed identity. This probe is now part of portable CI. [Process evidence](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/restore-process-faults.json)
+- The focused batched-pointer browser regression passed. The test protects the native-discovered swipe race.
+- A focused background-tab recycle/restart test passed: the active editor instance and source stayed intact, the removed tab disappeared, calendar/search counts updated, Undo restored the original note, and workspace restart retained the active page without reopening the recycled tab.
+- CI [41992453693](https://github.com/styayur/gitpad-plus/actions/runs/41992453693) passed at checkpoint `427b695`, with 47 Playwright, 49 Core, 52 Vitest and 23 release/provenance/transport tests plus Windows compilation and source-built Win2D drawing. The later `cc0d9d5` portable job also passed, including 48 browser cases and the real restore subprocess probe. The current browser suite has 49 tests. Complete CI must include the additional RPC/background-tab regressions; final-head results are tracked in the [PR checks](https://github.com/styayur/gitpad-plus/pull/6/checks), and older checkpoints are not substitutes.
+- Earlier local browser failures remain recorded: an image-case context teardown timeout after 44 passes (focused rerun passed), an early second-pane recycle attempted before its initial save (both safety cases passed after correcting setup), and a loopback navigation/startup timeout in a later focused run. Timeout limits were not raised to hide failures.
+- The updated Windows development build compiled with zero warnings/errors. Android product probe 3 and test instrumentation compiled and passed signature checks. Instrumentation is a separate test-only APK and must never be distributed as a product asset.
+
+Local detailed logs are retained under `artifacts/ui-v11-*` and the dedicated acceptance root `E:\GitPadPlus-Acceptance\ui-v11-20261105`. Final-head CI and final release-package checks remain separate.
+
+## Native Verified
+
+### Android
+
+API 36 / Android 16 x86_64 AVD `GitPadPlus_API36_Pixel7`, actual installed signed Release configuration, development stamp and non-AOT probe scope. Probe 3 is 19,133,707 bytes, SHA-256 `7ea54ca1d245a253cb600d28be3105e25166a16e37362751cbe191925d2bd55e`. The installed `base.apk` hash matched. Certificate SHA-256 remains `4fe4a85c853243d9d7c1b0dc421b5786f1bb89a91f22f8c691fe6840824e9fd0`. [Build identity](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/android-probe3-build-info.json)
+
+- Probe 2 passed actual 320px/393px single- and two-pane layout checks, including compact secondary controls, menu dismissal, real IME insets and zero CSS-pixel toolbar/viewport gap. At 320px, full viewport 716px became 457px with IME, leaving a 285px primary writing body. At 393px, 708px became 433px with a 261px body. Calendar targets were at least 44px. [320 geometry](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/android-probe2-320-ui-design.json), [393 split geometry](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/android-probe2-393-ui-two-pane.json)
+- Probe 3 passed real native vertical/short/complete swipes, explicit recycle, Undo, a second recycle, and Settings/Trash Restore. Raw Markdown and sidecar hashes before and after restoration were equal; the full loaded note, identity and metadata were equal. [Trash report](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/android-probe3-trash.json), [Undo frame](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/trash-native-recycled.png), [restored Trash frame](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/trash-native-restored.png)
+- Probe 3 passed native Bold touch with an active selection and visible IME. The text selection and editor instance survived, the toolbar stayed at the keyboard edge, selection links reconstructed correctly, and official toolbar disable/reactivate disposed/recreated its commands. Native folds, image decoding, source peek, persisted anchors and SQLite search also passed. The selection was established by the test before native touch, so this does not qualify Android selection-handle dragging. [Feature report](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/android-probe3-features.json)
+- Probe 3 passed four long-writing cases: 320px/393px, single/two-pane. Real native paste entered 201 paragraphs with Chinese, English, punctuation and newlines. The collapsed DOM caret remained in the final paragraph, visibly above status, with one toolbar at the actual IME edge. [320 split report](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/320-writing-end-two-pane.json), [320 split frame](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/320-writing-end-two-pane.png), [393 frame](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/393-writing-end.png)
+- Probe 3 passed fresh smoke, process restart, Activity recreation and background/resume with source content, block identities and plugin identity retained. [Smoke](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/smoke.json), [restart](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/smoke-restart.json), [recreation](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/smoke-recreate.json), [resume](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/smoke-resume.json)
+
+Failures were retained rather than overwritten. The initial probe-3 attempt timed out during cold WebView evaluation; the next input was blocked by a real Android System UI ANR dialog. A normal emulator reboot cleared that environment failure. Later test-only failures used an unavailable editor-internal view property, created a secondary note without refreshing UI choices, or started single-pane smoke with a restored split workspace. The harness now measures the DOM caret, creates fixtures through the existing UI and waits for split closure persistence. Corrected runs passed. [Retained attempts](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/retained-failures)
+
+Rendered review followed `interface-design` against the saved native frames and the existing Calm Precision tokens. The date track, plain note rows, quiet writing surface, compact title/actions and single command strip remain consistent. Status and Trash dialogs use the same surfaces and hierarchy. Native clipboard preview overlays visible in some frames belong to Android and are not product chrome. No new palette, decorative cards or global redesign was introduced. These are inspected development frames, not final-package visual acceptance.
+
+### Windows
+
+Computer Use clicked the real native X after a fresh target/screenshot observation. The user's later explicit Computer Use instruction superseded the earlier operator-only handoff. No terminal, browser, Codex or authentication UI was controlled. All vaults were synthetic.
+
+The corrected idle-host run used Windows build 26200, 16 logical processors, approximately 10.6 GiB initially free RAM and 1% captured CPU load. Android and builds were stopped. Product assembly SHA-256 `dab032b0661dd0ecbf2f392d79e6f30a1c4b52761c89c4552b1821cefe7d2956`. Each scenario retains its own environment, source hashes, trace and samples. The table measures the native close event to the kernel exit timestamp; physical mouse dispatch time is outside that boundary.
+
+| Scenario | Runs | Median ms | P95 ms | Max ms |
+|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| Empty | 5 | 444.65 | 508.98 | 508.98 |
+| Ordinary note, plugins enabled | 3 | 509.45 | 540.01 | 540.01 |
+| 10,000 source paragraphs | 3 | 256.09 | 281.40 | 281.40 |
+| Two panes | 3 | 601.92 | 652.24 | 652.24 |
+| 40 references to one small image | 5 | 481.54 | 736.37 | 736.37 |
+| Official plugins disabled | 3 | 500.85 | 567.99 | 567.99 |
+
+All 22 exit codes were zero, each had one close request, visibility was observed in every case, and all repeated-run Markdown/sidecar hashes were unchanged. Native close-event to `window.closed` was at most 24.58ms. These small sample sizes do not establish a population tail percentile. The image workload is 40 references to one small PNG, not 40 large independent photos. One image run captured the app and six owned WebView2 processes before closing; all seven were absent at the post-close observation. [Summary](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-exit-kernel/summary.json), [source pairs](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-exit-kernel/source-pair-comparison.json), [process-tree check](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-exit-kernel/images/process-tree-after-run3.json)
+
+The initial pre-load image-fixture hashes differed from the later saved pair; that first comparison is retained as changed. The corrected repeated-run evidence starts from the saved pair and makes no unchanged-byte claim for the first image initialization. The first recent-edit attempts had already auto-saved by the actual close event, so they do not qualify pending-save shutdown. The separate locked-source rounds establish that coverage with `Dirty=true` in the native trace.
+
+Three additional real native save-failure/retry rounds held an exclusive read lock on the synthetic source file. Editing produced visible SaveError. X kept the window and unsaved buffer open. Releasing the lock and clicking X again requested a flush with `Dirty=true`, received `save.flushed` with `Dirty=false`, and exited normally. The three recovery flushes took 810.50/728.16/910.20ms; retry-to-kernel-exit took 1287.56/1178.32/1385.58ms. Deliberate lock/operator waiting time is excluded from those recovery timings and must not be treated as shutdown performance. Restart through Core preserved all three inserted markers, the original prose (comparison ignores whitespace after marker removal), metadata, document/block UUIDs, valid source-pair hashes and searchable index. No pending save transaction was created while reads were blocked. [Recovery timings](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-save-blocked-recovery/recovery-timings.json), [integrity](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/exit-save-blocked-integrity.json), [SaveError frame](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-save-error-blocks-exit.png)
+
+The earlier samples include a 3835.90ms empty close and a 2614.84ms image close. They are retained. The first sampler used `HasExited`, could capture an initial hidden handle, and did not separate observer scheduling from the kernel timestamp. A calibration attempt also returned zero/1601 kernel exit times and is invalid for kernel-distribution claims. Correcting the observer is not an application latency fix. The corrected run did not reproduce the multi-second tail. The old slow traces place much of the delay after native window closure, and one after the managed `ProcessExit` record; this does not establish which native/runtime teardown or host-load condition caused it. Dispatcher summaries cover the observed app lifetime, including startup, and do not prove every close-path stall is absent. [Early sample](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-exit-baseline/earliest-empty-sample.json), [old image trace](docs/design/calm-precision/ui-v11/windows-exit-baseline/images-slow-trace.jsonl)
+
+## Not Verified
+
+- The reported intermittent multi-second Windows exit cause is unresolved. No application performance fix, eliminated UI-thread stall, production percentile or before/after improvement is claimed. A reproducible slow event with native/runtime profiling remains needed before choosing a teardown change.
+- Physical mouse dispatch latency, exhaustive WebView2 residue across every run, sustained repeated-close reentrancy, and save completion under every external conflict were not established by these samples.
+- Chinese IME composition, Android selection-handle dragging, rotation, three-button navigation, all accessibility/font scaling combinations and physical-device performance remain unverified. Clipboard Unicode input has a narrower scope.
+- Final universal AOT Android and distributable Windows packages from an accepted exact main SHA remain unqualified. Development probes do not satisfy final package provenance/runtime gates.
+- Final exact-main source/license/security evidence and full 17-gate package qualification must bind to the final packages. Branch CI and initial checkpoint results are not substitutes for exact-main release evidence.
+
+## Blocked
+
+There is no current desktop-input authorization blocker. Native tests use synthetic vaults and the existing signing identity. Publication remains gated by final source/package qualification and the unresolved Windows long-tail investigation. No release approval is inferred from development-probe success.
+
+## Release Impact
+
+Both affected platform packages and their native evidence must be regenerated after final integration. The existing public alpha assets and annotated tag remain tied to their earlier accepted source. Do not replace them with branch probes or retag that release.

@@ -0,0 +1,77 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
+using System.Collections.Concurrent;
+using System.Diagnostics;
+using System.Text.Json;
+using System.Text.Json.Serialization;
+
+namespace GitPadPlus.App;
+
+// Opt-in measurements contain phase names and timings only. Buffering avoids
+// filesystem work on the UI thread while the window is closing.
+internal static class ExitDiagnostics
+{
+    private static readonly string? destination = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE");
+    private static readonly ConcurrentQueue<ExitMeasurement> events = new();
+    private static readonly long started = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
+
+    static ExitDiagnostics()
+    {
+        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(destination)) return;
+        AppDomain.CurrentDomain.ProcessExit += (_, _) =>
+        {
+            Record("process.exit");
+            try
+            {
+                File.WriteAllLines(destination, events.Select(entry => JsonSerializer.Serialize(entry, ExitJsonContext.Default.ExitMeasurement)));
+            }
+            catch (Exception exception) when (exception is IOException or UnauthorizedAccessException)
+            {
+                // Diagnostic output must not prevent application shutdown.
+            }
+        };
+    }
+
+    internal static void Record(string phase, bool? dirty = null)
+    {
+        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(destination)) return;
+        events.Enqueue(new ExitMeasurement(phase, Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(started).TotalMilliseconds,
+            Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId, dirty, Stopwatch.GetTimestamp()));
+    }
+
+    internal static Action ObserveDispatcher(Microsoft.UI.Dispatching.DispatcherQueue dispatcher)
+    {
+        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(destination)) return () => { };
+        var stopped = 0;
+        var pending = 0;
+        var count = 0;
+        var maximum = 0d;
+        // Only one outstanding probe. Work stays bounded even during a stall.
+        var timer = new Timer(_ =>
+        {
+            if (Volatile.Read(ref stopped) != 0 || Interlocked.Exchange(ref pending, 1) != 0) return;
+            var queued = Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
+            if (!dispatcher.TryEnqueue(() =>
+            {
+                if (Volatile.Read(ref stopped) == 0)
+                {
+                    maximum = Math.Max(maximum, Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(queued).TotalMilliseconds);
+                    count++;
+                }
+                Volatile.Write(ref pending, 0);
+            })) Volatile.Write(ref pending, 0);
+        }, null, 100, 100);
+        return () =>
+        {
+            if (Interlocked.Exchange(ref stopped, 1) != 0) return;
+            timer.Dispose();
+            events.Enqueue(new ExitMeasurement("dispatcher.summary", Stopwatch.GetElapsedTime(started).TotalMilliseconds,
+                Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId, null, Stopwatch.GetTimestamp(), maximum, count));
+        };
+    }
+}
+
+internal sealed record ExitMeasurement(string Phase, double ElapsedMs, int Thread, bool? Dirty, long Timestamp,
+    double? MaximumDispatchDelayMs = null, int? DispatchSamples = null);
+
+[JsonSerializable(typeof(ExitMeasurement))]
+internal partial class ExitJsonContext : JsonSerializerContext;

@@ -9,3 +9,18 @@ Web modules separate the Markdown AST/source mapper, editor state/identity, anch
 DocumentSession is a per-note single-writer queue. It snapshots edits, sends the previous acknowledged revision/hash, retains a newer buffer during delayed saves and reports errors without dropping content. Native requests are serialized at the WebView boundary. A timeout/cancellation cannot undo a committed native operation; reload before retrying uncertain writes.
 
 Block tracking traverses nested block nodes and persists structural paths in the sidecar. Invertible identity steps participate in actual ProseMirror history so Undo/Redo restores identities without a content-keyed cache; ordinary copies allocate fresh UUIDv7 IDs. Each rendered editor session owns a distinct DOM instance. Two distinct notes can be edited in separate panes; the workspace stores the secondary note ID. Recovery explicitly archives all conflicting inputs and any open editor buffer before applying selected Markdown. Portable/browser and native evidence are recorded separately.
+
+## Local trash restoration
+
+Protocol version 1 adds two shell RPC methods, documents.trash and
+documents.restore. The former returns NoteSummary entries from retained
+tombstones. The latter accepts an id and returns the original Note after
+restoring the exact source pair. Plugin capability grants are unchanged.
+
+Restore rejects an occupied active identity before recording its intent. A
+restoring.json record binds the retained Markdown and sidecar hashes. Restart
+recovery completes that intent before applying old deletion tombstones. After
+both original files validate, the complete tombstone folder moves atomically
+under .gitpad/restored, and the disposable index is rebuilt. The archive
+preserves the previous deletion transaction. Restoring a different source over
+an occupied identity raises a conflict and retains the source copies.

index 0000000..547da67
--- /dev/null
+++ b/scripts/measure-windows-exit.ps1
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
+[CmdletBinding()]
+param(
+    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Executable,
+    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$VaultPath,
+    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$OutputDirectory,
+    [string]$Scenario='empty',
+    [ValidateRange(3,30)][int]$Runs=5
+)
+$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
+$exe=(Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $Executable).Path
+$output=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath($OutputDirectory)
+$vault=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath($VaultPath)
+if (Get-Process GitPadPlus.App -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object {!$_.HasExited}) {throw 'Close the existing GitPad+ process before measuring.'}
+if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $output) {throw 'Choose a fresh measurement directory.'}
+if ($output.StartsWith($vault+[IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar,[StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) {throw 'Keep diagnostics outside the test vault.'}
+New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $output | Out-Null
+Add-Type @'
+using System;
+using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
+public static class ExitWindowObservation {
+    [DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool IsWindowVisible(IntPtr window);
+    public static long[] ClockAnchor() {
+        long bestStart=0, bestEnd=0, bestUtc=0, best=long.MaxValue;
+        for(int i=0;i<8;i++) {
+            long start=System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
+            long utc=DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks;
+            long end=System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch.GetTimestamp();
+            if(end-start<best){best=end-start;bestStart=start;bestEnd=end;bestUtc=utc;}
+        }
+        return new[]{bestStart+(bestEnd-bestStart)/2,bestUtc,best};
+    }
+}
+'@
+$os=Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem
+$cpu=Get-CimInstance Win32_Processor
+[ordered]@{
+    capturedAt=[DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow
+    osBuild=$os.BuildNumber
+    freePhysicalKilobytes=$os.FreePhysicalMemory
+    logicalProcessors=[Environment]::ProcessorCount
+    processorLoadPercent=($cpu | Measure-Object -Property LoadPercentage -Average).Average
+} | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $output 'environment.json') -Encoding utf8
+$results=@()
+$exeHash=(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $exe).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
+$assemblyHash=(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath (Join-Path (Split-Path -Parent $exe) 'GitPadPlus.App.dll')).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
+foreach ($run in 1..$Runs) {
+    $trace=Join-Path $output "trace-$run.jsonl"
+    $previousVault=$env:GITPAD_ACCEPTANCE_VAULT
+    $previousTrace=$env:GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE
+    try {
+        $env:GITPAD_ACCEPTANCE_VAULT=$vault
+        $env:GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE=$trace
+        $process=Start-Process -FilePath $exe -WorkingDirectory (Split-Path -Parent $exe) -PassThru
+    } finally {
+        $env:GITPAD_ACCEPTANCE_VAULT=$previousVault
+        $env:GITPAD_EXIT_TRACE=$previousTrace
+    }
+    $startup=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
+    while (!$process.HasExited -and !$process.MainWindowHandle -and $startup.Elapsed.TotalSeconds -lt 60) {
+        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 20
+        $process.Refresh()
+    }
+    if ($process.HasExited -or !$process.MainWindowHandle) {throw 'Native window did not appear. Preserve this failed attempt.'}
+    $handle=$process.MainWindowHandle
+    Write-Host "Run $run of $Runs. Prepare the $Scenario scenario, then close the native window using its X button."
+    $observation=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
+    # Correlate the monotonic native event clock with the kernel's ExitTime.
+    # Poll completion can be delayed by the observer's own scheduling/GC.
+    $clockAnchor=[ExitWindowObservation]::ClockAnchor()
+    $anchorTimestamp=$clockAnchor[0]
+    $anchorUtcTicks=$clockAnchor[1]
+    $hidden=$null
+    $lastVisible=$null
+    while (!$process.WaitForExit(0) -and $observation.Elapsed.TotalMinutes -lt 10) {
+        if (!$hidden) {
+            $currentHandle=$process.MainWindowHandle
+            if($currentHandle -ne [IntPtr]::Zero){$handle=$currentHandle}
+            $observed=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::GetTimestamp()
+            if ([ExitWindowObservation]::IsWindowVisible($handle)) {$lastVisible=$observed}
+            elseif($null -ne $lastVisible) {$hidden=$observed}
+        }
+        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 10
+        $process.Refresh()
+    }
+    $ended=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::GetTimestamp()
+    if (!$process.WaitForExit(0)) {throw 'The observation ended with the app still running. No process was terminated.'}
+    if (!(Test-Path -LiteralPath $trace)) {throw 'Exit trace missing. Use a build with opt-in exit diagnostics.'}
+    $events=@(Get-Content -LiteralPath $trace | ForEach-Object {$_ | ConvertFrom-Json})
+    $close=$events | Where-Object Phase -eq 'close.requested' | Select-Object -First 1
+    if (!$close.Timestamp) {throw 'The trace has no close-request timestamp.'}
+    $frequency=[Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::Frequency
+    $exitUtc=$process.ExitTime.ToUniversalTime()
+    if($exitUtc.Year -lt 2020){throw 'Kernel exit timestamp is unavailable. Preserve the attempt without reporting a distribution.'}
+    $kernelExitTimestamp=$anchorTimestamp+($exitUtc.Ticks-$anchorUtcTicks)*$frequency/[TimeSpan]::TicksPerSecond
+    $clockEnd=[ExitWindowObservation]::ClockAnchor()
+    $clockDriftMs=($clockEnd[1]-$anchorUtcTicks)/[TimeSpan]::TicksPerMillisecond-1000*($clockEnd[0]-$anchorTimestamp)/$frequency
+    $visibleDelay=$null
+    $residual=$null
+    if ($hidden -and $hidden -ge $close.Timestamp) {
+        $visibleDelay=1000*($hidden-$close.Timestamp)/$frequency
+        $residual=1000*($ended-$hidden)/$frequency
+    }
+    $results+= [ordered]@{
+        run=$run
+        scenario=$Scenario
+        executableSha256=$exeHash
+        assemblySha256=$assemblyHash
+        closeRequestToProcessExitMs=1000*($ended-$close.Timestamp)/$frequency
+        kernelCloseRequestToProcessExitMs=1000*($kernelExitTimestamp-$close.Timestamp)/$frequency
+        observerSchedulingLagMs=1000*($ended-$kernelExitTimestamp)/$frequency
+        clockCorrelationDriftMs=$clockDriftMs
+        clockAnchorUncertaintyMs=1000*($clockAnchor[2]+$clockEnd[2])/$frequency
+        processExitUtc=$exitUtc
+        closeRequestToWindowHiddenMs=$visibleDelay
+        windowHiddenToProcessExitMs=$residual
+        windowHiddenObserved=($null -ne $visibleDelay)
+        windowHiddenToExitUpperBoundMs=if($null -ne $lastVisible){1000*($ended-$lastVisible)/$frequency}else{$null}
+        exitCode=$process.ExitCode
+        closeRequests=@($events | Where-Object Phase -eq 'close.requested').Count
+        unsavedAtClose=$close.Dirty
+        trace=Split-Path -Leaf $trace
+    }
+    $results | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $output 'samples.json') -Encoding utf8
+}
+$latencies=@($results.closeRequestToProcessExitMs | Sort-Object)
+$kernelLatencies=@($results.kernelCloseRequestToProcessExitMs | Sort-Object)
+$middle=[int][Math]::Floor($latencies.Count/2)
+$median=$latencies[$middle]
+if ($latencies.Count%2 -eq 0) {$median=($latencies[$middle-1]+$latencies[$middle])/2}
+[ordered]@{
+    scenario=$Scenario
+    runs=$Runs
+    medianMs=$median
+    p95Ms=$latencies[[int][Math]::Ceiling($latencies.Count*.95)-1]
+    maximumMs=$latencies[-1]
+    kernelMedianMs=if($Runs%2){$kernelLatencies[$middle]}else{($kernelLatencies[$middle-1]+$kernelLatencies[$middle])/2}
+    kernelP95Ms=$kernelLatencies[[int][Math]::Ceiling($Runs*.95)-1]
+    kernelMaximumMs=$kernelLatencies[-1]
+    scope='Native close event to OS process exit, sampled every 10 ms. Operator clicks X. Physical click dispatch latency and UI-thread stalls require separate observation.'
+} | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $output 'distribution.json') -Encoding utf8

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
+namespace GitPadPlus.Core;
+
+public sealed partial class VaultStore
+{
+    public NoteSummary[] ListTrash()
+    {
+        lock (gate)
+        {
+            return Directory.EnumerateDirectories(Safe(".gitpad", "trash"))
+                .Where(folder => File.Exists(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "deleted.json")))
+                .Select(folder =>
+                {
+                    var marker = Read<DeleteMarker>(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "deleted.json"));
+                    var header = Frontmatter.Decode(File.ReadAllText(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "document.md"), Utf8)).Header;
+                    if (header.Id != marker.Id) throw new RecoveryRequiredException("Trash document identity mismatch.");
+                    return new NoteSummary(header.Id, header.Date, header.Title, header.Tags);
+                }).ToArray();
+        }
+    }
+
+    public Note Restore(Guid id)
+    {
+        lock (gate)
+        {
+            var folder = Safe(".gitpad", "trash", Identity.Require(id).ToString());
+            var marker = Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "restoring.json");
+            if (!File.Exists(marker))
+            {
+                if (File.Exists(Markdown(id)) || File.Exists(AnchorPath(id)))
+                {
+                    // A completed source-pair restore may lose its response or
+                    // fail while rebuilding the disposable index. Accept only
+                    // an exact replay of a retained committed transaction.
+                    var archive = Safe(".gitpad", "restored", id.ToString());
+                    if (!Directory.Exists(folder) && Directory.Exists(archive)
+                        && File.Exists(Markdown(id)) && File.Exists(AnchorPath(id)))
+                    {
+                        var markdownHash = RestoreHash(Markdown(id));
+                        var sidecarHash = RestoreHash(AnchorPath(id));
+                        foreach (var entry in Directory.EnumerateDirectories(archive))
+                        {
+                            var retained = Read<RestoreMarker>(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, entry), "restoring.json"));
+                            if (retained.Id != id || retained.MarkdownHash != markdownHash
+                                || retained.SidecarHash != sidecarHash) continue;
+                            RebuildIndex();
+                            return Load(id);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    throw new RevisionConflictException("An active document already occupies this identity.");
+                }
+                var deleted = Read<DeleteMarker>(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "deleted.json"));
+                var text = File.ReadAllText(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "document.md"), Utf8);
+                var sidecar = Read<Sidecar>(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "sidecar.json"));
+                if (deleted.Id != id || Frontmatter.Decode(text).Header.Id != id || sidecar.DocumentId != id
+                    || sidecar.Revision != deleted.Revision || sidecar.ContentHash != Identity.Hash(text))
+                    throw new RecoveryRequiredException("Incomplete or inconsistent trash source pair.");
+                DurableWrite(marker, Json(new RestoreMarker(id, RestoreHash(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "document.md")),
+                    RestoreHash(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "sidecar.json")))));
+                checkpoint?.Invoke("RestoreStaged");
+            }
+            FinishRestore(folder);
+            checkpoint?.Invoke("RestoreCommitted");
+            RebuildIndex();
+            return Load(id);
+        }
+    }
+
+    private void FinishRestore(string folder)
+    {
+        var restore = Read<RestoreMarker>(Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "restoring.json"));
+        if (Path.GetFileName(folder) != Identity.Require(restore.Id).ToString())
+            throw new RecoveryRequiredException("Restore transaction identity mismatch.");
+        RestoreFile(folder, "document.md", Markdown(restore.Id), restore.MarkdownHash);
+        checkpoint?.Invoke("RestoreMarkdownReplaced");
+        RestoreFile(folder, "sidecar.json", AnchorPath(restore.Id), restore.SidecarHash);
+        checkpoint?.Invoke("RestoreSidecarReplaced");
+        _ = Load(restore.Id);
+        // Moving the whole tombstone directory commits the restore atomically.
+        // A crash cannot expose the old deletion marker without its restore marker.
+        var archive = Safe(".gitpad", "restored", restore.Id.ToString());
+        Directory.CreateDirectory(archive);
+        Directory.Move(folder, Path.Combine(archive, Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")));
+    }
+
+    private static string RestoreHash(string path)
+    {
+        using var stream = File.OpenRead(path);
+        return Convert.ToHexStringLower(System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256.HashData(stream));
+    }
+
+    private void RestoreFile(string folder, string name, string target, string expectedHash)
+    {
+        if (File.Exists(target))
+        {
+            if (RestoreHash(target) != expectedHash)
+                throw new RecoveryRequiredException("Restore target changed; retained copies require review.");
+            return;
+        }
+        var source = Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), name);
+        if (RestoreHash(source) != expectedHash)
+            throw new RecoveryRequiredException("Retained restore source changed.");
+        var staged = Safe(Path.GetRelativePath(root, folder), "restore-" + name);
+        using (var input = File.OpenRead(source))
+        using (var output = new FileStream(staged, FileMode.Create, FileAccess.Write, FileShare.None))
+        {
+            input.CopyTo(output);
+            output.Flush(flushToDisk: true);
+        }
+        File.Move(staged, target);
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,55 @@
+name: Stacked PR CodeQL
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+concurrency:
+  group: stacked-codeql-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  analyze:
+    # Default setup covers main/protected targets. Stacked feature targets need
+    # an independent scan; retain its SARIF without conflicting with default setup.
+    if: github.base_ref != github.event.repository.default_branch
+    name: CodeQL stacked (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        language: [actions, javascript-typescript, python, rust]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
+        if: matrix.language == 'rust'
+      - run: npm ci
+        if: matrix.language == 'javascript-typescript'
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
+        with:
+          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
+          build-mode: none
+      - name: Analyze exact PR HEAD
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
+        with:
+          output: codeql-results
+          upload: never
+          upload-database: false
+      - name: Check analysis results
+        run: node scripts/codeql_results_gate.mjs codeql-results
+      - name: Retain SARIF
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: codeql-stacked-${{ matrix.language }}
+          path: codeql-results/*.sarif
+          if-no-files-found: error

The resolved concept opens an overview with prerequisites, objectives, an ordered learning path, a native guided lesson, external search resources, textbook metadata and related/next concepts. There are **four supported profiles and three lessons**, not profiles for every ontology concept. Unsupported concepts retain their ordinary search/graph/resource experience with an explicit learning fallback.

+# Query Resolver v2
+
+Prepared for 0.4.0-alpha.3. This implementation is offline and deterministic.
+It is still a draft maturity step: development exact accuracy is 95.15%, but
+holdout exact accuracy is 69.09%. The 26.06 percentage-point gap is visible in
+the benchmark and is not fixed by copying holdout phrases into production.
+
+```text
+Raw Query
+  ↓
+Normalizer (mechanical Unicode/script conversion)
+  ↓
+Lexical / Symbolic Parser
+  ↓
+Candidate Generator (indexed vocabulary + bounded typo recovery)
+  ↓
+Deterministic Ranker / overlapping-span constraints
+  ↓
+Ambiguity / Abstention
+  ↓
+Canonical Concept IDs
+  ↓
+ConceptSession → Workbench
+```
+
+## Public contract and ownership
+
+`src/query/resolve.ts` exports `resolveQuery(raw): QueryResolution`. Its typed
+contract contains normalizedQuery, groups, conceptIds, ranked candidates,
+status, heuristic confidence, evidence, residualTerms and a reason. Candidates
+contain integer scores, evidence, matched terms and penalties. Confidence is a
+score divided by 100, not a calibrated probability. It is not displayed as a
+percentage in the UI. `explanations.ts` supplies a development-only helper with
+tokens and the full resolution; it is not imported by the normal UI.
+
+The 494 canonical concepts and their aliases are unchanged. The query lexicon
+is a separate 37-entry resource. Resource annotation still uses ontology field
+matching only; colloquial and typo rules do not annotate provider resources.
+Resource URL fields never enter candidate scoring or semantic annotation.
+
+`normalizeConcepts()` and `parseAndExpand()` remain compatibility wrappers.
+`projectConceptResolution()` expands only the IDs selected by Resolver v2 into
+the original multilingual resource-search variants and explicit exploratory
+edges. Universal Search consumes ranked accepted candidates from this same
+resolution. Ambiguous results expose only concept choices, without deriving
+capabilities until the user chooses. Unknown results keep ordinary resource
+search; they do not open a ConceptSession. There is no second fuzzy resolver.
+
+## Normalization and scripts
+
+Normalization maps reviewed mathematical characters before native NFKC, then
+folds case, selected traditional characters, whitespace, punctuation, apostrophes
+and dash/minus variants. Superscript powers retain `^2` / `^3` structure.
+Greek symbols such as ω/λ/φ/π become omega/lambda/phi/pi tokens. Multiplication
+and cross-product structure remain present for the symbolic layer.
+
+For example, `Ｆｏｕｒｉｅｒ` becomes `fourier`; `∇×F` becomes `∇×f`;
+`轉動的動量` becomes `转动的动量`, never `angular momentum`. Normalization is
+idempotent on the supported inputs.
+
+`rules.json` contains a manually reviewed orthographic character table.
+Aligned regional labels must **not** generate this table: 電位/电势 and other
+regional terminology are semantically equivalent phrases, not character
+conversions. Ambiguous 後/發/髮/乾/幹/係/臺/裡 are preserved. Complete canonical
+EN, zh-CN and zh-TW labels are independently indexed; the four historical
+spellings preserve the existing reviewed source metadata. Tests verify that
+位相, 能力, 分裂, 波, 定理 and other unrelated text are not rewritten.
+
+## Lexicon, abbreviations and Chinese scaffolding
+
+Every lexicon entry names a pattern, canonical IDs, kind, language, confidence,
+provenance and reason. Historical entries cite the existing 数理化自学丛书
+物理（第二册）§1.1/§1.3 metadata. This stores only short terminology and source
+references, not textbook prose or a claim to ownership of those phrases.
+
+Curated groups include rotational momentum, spring stiffness/motion,
+time-derivative descriptions, circulation/steepest ascent, mixed-language
+transform names and standard STEM initialisms. Entries derived from development
+examples are marked `benchmark-generalized` where applicable. Their coverage
+does not amount to general Chinese NLP.
+
+Scaffolding such as 怎么算/是什么/怎么理解 is removed from **unmatched residual
+text after candidate generation**. This preserves concept-bearing phrases such
+as 振动的位相 and 速度的变化率. Remaining content imposes a large penalty rather
+than being silently discarded. `面积怎么变` requires an independently matched
+linear-transformation or matrix context; it cannot independently select a
+determinant. `线性变换面积怎么变` selects both concepts.
+
+Abbreviations require token boundaries. A CJK neighbor is permitted for an
+abbreviation in a mixed-language query; leftover unrelated content still causes
+abstention. FT has explicit competing Fourier-topic/transform interpretations:
+it is ambiguous and yields no accepted IDs. The prior golden case is explicitly
+migrated; FT inside left/after remains impossible. Exact canonical curl/phase/
+wave labels still resolve. No generic correction is attempted on ≤3-character
+tokens.
+
+## Indexed candidates, typo recovery and scoring
+
+Initialization builds an initial-character vocabulary index and a word-count
+index of Latin typo phrases. Normalized duplicate labels merge deterministically;
+canonical spellings take precedence over incidental synonym collisions. Query
+lexicon ambiguity remains explicit. Reusable `conservation of N` → `N
+conservation` composition is generated from canonical labels, outside ontology.
+
+Exact and structural matches precede typo recovery. Latin token/phrase boundaries
+are mandatory; CJK permits explicit, finite lexical substrings. Single-character
+canonical labels require boundaries, preventing 波 from matching 波士顿. Typo
+recovery uses only complete Latin tokens/phrases up to six words, with exactly
+one changed word and one insertion/deletion/substitution/adjacent transposition.
+Both changed words must exceed three characters. It does not scan fuzzy arbitrary
+substrings. `momemtum`, `fourrier transform` and `determinent` have bounded-typo
+evidence. Unrecognized surrounding words cannot create a confident recovery.
+
+| Evidence | Integer weight |
+| --- | ---: |
+| Canonical label / canonical ID | 100 |
+| Ontology alias | 96 |
+| Curated/historical query lexicon | round(92 × entry confidence) |
+| Formula pattern | 90 |
+| Symbolic operator / generated conservation composition | 88 |
+| Abbreviation | 86 |
+| Bounded typo | 76 |
+
+Longer matching spans claim their component terms before shorter spans. This
+prevents angular momentum from independently emitting momentum, while explicit
+`动量与角动量` keeps both. Independent spans become AND concept groups; safe
+multilingual equivalents within a concept remain OR variants. A whole structural
+identity is interpreted as a unit before lexical components.
+
+Unexplained letter/number content subtracts 45; competing interpretations subtract
+10. Acceptance requires score ≥70 and an eight-point margin between competing
+meanings on the **same span**. Independent requested concepts do not compete
+against one another. Ties use canonical ID ordering, never incidental array
+order. Ambiguous queries return no accepted IDs. Unknown queries expose rejected
+candidates for debugging but cannot create canonical navigation.
+
+## Restricted symbolic and formula parsing
+
+Shared, anchored token patterns recognize ∇×F, ∇·F, ∇f, named grad/div/curl/det
+operators, derivative notation, educational integrals, determinant bars,
+eigenpair identities and selected formulas. `Av=λv` proposes eigenvalue and
+eigenvector; the variable must agree on both sides. `Av=λu` does not count.
+
+Formula patterns cover F=ma, F=-kx, p=mv, L=r×p, E=mc², V=IR, the ellipse standard
+equation and selected harmonic motion identities. Recognized equations preserve
+required variable relationships. They are a finite grammar, not a CAS, and do
+not promise algebraic equivalence or arbitrary notation. F=-kx chooses Hooke's
+law; a standalone second derivative is a derivative, not by itself an ODE.
+
+## Safety and parity
+
+The resolver bounds input at 512 UTF-16 units, parentheses at depth 32, and typo
+phrase length at six words. Oversized input, malformed Unicode in JS, unbalanced
+parentheses and incomplete structures gracefully abstain. The flat patterns
+have no evaluation, code generation, recursive expression expansion, arbitrary
+functions or remote calls. Normal search syntax parsing is also bounded before
+token scanning. Production sources are checked for adversarial-fixture imports
+and benchmark IDs. Rust test-only includes are compiled under `cfg(test)`.
+
+Rust `search/resolver` mirrors normalization, indexing, candidates, span
+constraints, integer scores, ranking and evidence. Both consume the same JSON.
+`regex` was already present transitively and is now declared directly;
+`unicode-normalization` is needed because Rust std lacks NFKC. It is dual
+MIT/Apache-2.0 (locked at 0.1.25) and adds no frontend package. Native JS NFKC
+and the Rust Unicode tables are verified against the shared corpus; arbitrary
+future Unicode-version differences are not claimed to be exhaustively covered.
+
+`npm run test:parity` retains the original search ranking/annotation parity and
+adds 1,783 complete resolver contracts: representative mechanisms, 1,482 exact
+canonical labels, malformed structures and all 220 frozen adversarial cases.
+Scores, evidence, normalized groups, statuses and residuals compare exactly.
+Canonical punctuation/idempotence and orthographic safety are also tested in
+Rust's normal test suite.
+
+## Benchmarks, gates and extension
+
+The original 220 queries and independent gold remain unchanged. Every fourth
+case within each category becomes the separate holdout (165 development, 55
+holdout). The split was written before inspecting development data. Holdout was
+first evaluated after rules froze; the only later pattern edits correct variable
+consistency and the meaning of a standalone derivative, independently of held
+queries. Future changes must treat this already evaluated holdout honestly and
+add a separately reviewed new holdout if tuning on its failures.
+
+Metrics name exactConceptSetAccuracy, top1ConceptAccuracy and
+negativeRejectionRate explicitly. Top-1 uses the highest-ranked **accepted**
+candidate on positives; abstentions count as failures. Baseline first-resolved
+accuracy used alphabetically sorted old IDs and is not a calibrated ranker.
+Mechanism counts are nonexclusive and only include exact successful positives.
+Language, category and a fixed category-level difficulty rubric are reported.
+Unknown abstention uses negative gold; independent ambiguity-status accuracy
+uses the compact FT contract, one case, not the 220 concept-set gold.
+
+Hard gates retain canonical quality, full parity, zero hard false positives,
+negative rejection at least the old 67.86%, and holdout no more than five points
+below its measured v1 40% baseline. Targets include overall/category improvement
+and a dev/holdout gap ≤20 points. The first experimental gap assertion failed;
+it was separated from the **regression** gate, and remains a loud reporting
+failure. Draft status is retained because 26.06 points exceeds that quality
+target. No benchmark thresholds or gold were modified to conceal a failure.
+
+Artifacts report lexicon size, zero ontology-alias growth, normalized exact
+lexicon/query overlap, accepted mechanisms, false positives and abstentions.
+Node performance uses 3,300 fixed development queries and reports cold import
+initialization, median/p95/max, batch time, heap and static-data size. It does not
+claim browser latency. See [measured report](audits/v0.4-query-resolver-report.md).
+
+To extend: document a reviewed phrase/rule and provenance outside ontology; add
+independent positive and near-negative cases; validate all canonical mappings;
+run both language implementations and full parity; measure on development and
+then a new held set. Do not copy benchmark IDs or queries into runtime, weaken
+boundary guards, or grow ontology merely to recognize a query.

+# Concept-driven visual learning
+
+## Workbench integration (0.4.0-alpha.2)
+
+The long learning panel is now a [Concept Workbench](workbench-architecture.md).
+ConceptSession is the canonical context; Learn owns the ordered path, Visualize
+gives the lesson the main area, Resources resolves direct Concept ID annotations,
+and Inspector follows the current step or resource. Ctrl/Cmd+K opens registered
+contextual commands; Ctrl/Cmd+L focuses search. The three lesson definitions are
+independent dynamic imports, while the numeric player and renderer are shared.
+GuidedStep additionally supports optional misconception, observation, cause and
+consequence fields. JSXGraph's JessieCode and Geonext expression boundaries both
+fail closed; final production assets have AST/provenance regression checks.
+
+The following sections document the retained v0.4 lesson model and mathematics.
+
+The v0.4.0-alpha.1 MVP adds native guided lessons to the existing Web and Tauri search client. It preserves provider search, ranking, preview policies, favorites, history, workspaces and translation. Search for **简谐振动 / simple harmonic motion**, **椭圆 / ellipse**, or **行列式 / determinant** and click the resolved concept's **Learn visually** action. A concept can be learned even when the current provider filter returns no resources.
+
+## Architecture
+
+```text
+Ontology — what the concept is
+  ↓ existing Concept ID and query resolver (TypeScript / Rust parity)
+Learning Registry — how to understand it
+  ↓ prerequisite IDs, objectives, ordered path, references, visualization IDs
+Visualization Registry — reviewed teaching definitions
+  ↓ localized steps, equations, invariants, parameters, presets, scene descriptions
+Guided State Machine — explicit learner actions and bounded numeric state
+  ↓ numeric scene frame (points, paths, polygons, arrows, readouts)
+VisualizationRenderer → JSXGraphRenderer — drawing and pointer input
+```
+
+`src/lib/concepts.json` remains the canonical ontology. Only four missing concepts were added: ellipse, Hooke's law, spring constant and mechanical equilibrium. The existing `newton-s-second-law` ID is reused. The Chinese synonyms 简谐振动 / 簡諧振動 were moved from `harmonic-oscillator` to `simple-harmonic-motion`; the oscillator keeps its modern labels and other synonyms. This intentional correction also updates the glossary expectation, without removing an assertion.
+
+`src/learning/types.ts` defines `ConceptLearningProfile`, `LearningStage`, `TextbookReference`, `HistoricalAlias` and `LocalizedText`. The small registry has **four supported profiles**: SHM, ellipse, linear transformation and determinant. The last two share one lesson. Paths refer to a visualization ID and a step ID; registry tests check all links and ontology edges. Unsupported concepts open an overview with their ontology prerequisites, related concepts and external-resource search. No empty profiles or placeholder animations are generated.
+
+## Teaching definitions and renderer boundary
+
+`GuidedVisualizationDefinition` in `src/visualizations/types.ts` declares the title, concept IDs, kind, renderer, steps, bounded parameters and presets. Each `GuidedStep` supplies three-language title/explanation/invariant, TeX equations, scene stage, visible controls and highlighted primitive IDs. An invariant expresses the structure the learner should recognize, including whether it applies only while parameters are fixed.
+
+`definitions.ts` contains all authored lesson content, outside JSX. `math.ts` contains analytic models; `scenes.ts` turns those models into `SceneFrame` data. Models do not import React or JSXGraph. A scene frame has a numeric bounding box, labeled numeric geometry and readouts. `VisualizationRenderer` selects the adapter; only `renderers/` imports JSXGraph. Future adapters would implement the same numeric-frame boundary and extend the renderer discriminator; this MVP implements only JSXGraph in 2D.
+
+Boards are initialized once per primitive structure/theme. Updates change point coordinates and data curves, rather than recreating the board every animation frame. Board, resize handlers, animation callbacks and media/theme observers are disposed on unmount. Trace history is bounded at 600 samples. The ellipse's P is projected to its locus after a pointer drag; labeled sliders provide an equivalent keyboard route.
+
+## Pedagogical state machine
+
+`stateMachine.ts` owns the step index, paused/playing/completed state, elapsed physical time, normalized parameters and visited locus points. Its pure reducer handles `seek`, `play`, `pause`, `restart`, `tick` and `parameters`.
+
+- Previous/Next and path entries change the teaching state, reset its clock and pause. Playback never silently advances the learner to another step.
+- Play/Pause animate or freeze the current scene. Completed one-shot scenes restart on Play. Static steps have playback disabled.
+- Parameter changes pause playback and establish a new system. Restart resets the lesson to its first step and default parameters.
+- SHM playback uses physical time and `ω = √(k/m)`; the release stops at the first equilibrium crossing and the periodicity step stops after a full period.
+- Ellipse tracing records only visited points, clearing when a or c changes. Later steps show the complete locus.
+- Transformation playback interpolates `B(s) = (1−s)I + sA`; the progress slider can inspect any intermediate matrix. This interpolation can pass through a singular B even when A is invertible. Readouts distinguish the target A from the displayed B.
+- Hidden tabs pause. Frame deltas are bounded, avoiding large jumps after a stall. A change to reduced-motion preference pauses immediately and disables playback.
+
+## Implemented lessons
+
+| Lesson | Guided states | Controls / structure |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| SHM (10) | Equilibrium → displacement → restoring force → Newton II → release → equilibrium crossing → opposite displacement → periodicity → equation/phase → energy | Drag the mass in the displacement/force stages; A, k, m, φ sliders; spring/mass view, force/velocity/acceleration vectors, x(t), K/U/E bars. `F = −kx`, `a = −ω²x`, `x = A cos(ωt+φ)`, `K+U = ½kA²`. |
+| Ellipse (7) | Foci → P and distances → constant sum → traced locus → a/b/c → right triangle → standard equation | Drag P, or use θ; a and c sliders enforce `0 ≤ c < a` (a 0.1 safety margin). `PF₁+PF₂ = 2a`, `b² = a²−c²`, `x²/a²+y²/b² = 1`. The c=0 circle limit is supported. |
+| Linear transformation / determinant (7) | Identity → basis images → continuous grid transform → parallelogram → area → orientation/collapse → exploration | Four matrix-entry sliders, progress, rotation/scaling/shear/reflection/singular presets. Original dashed grid and square remain as references. Columns determine the basis images; `|det(A)|` is the area ratio and its sign is the orientation. Corner order makes orientation observable without relying on color. |
+
+SHM assumes an ideal horizontal spring with no friction, and no damping or forcing. Vectors use disclosed display scales; readouts give the exact SI values. Energy stays constant during motion with fixed parameters; changing A or k changes the total energy. In displacement stages the mass is held to the positive side before release; the opposite-side state demonstrates compression and force reversal.
+
+## Textbook references and historical terminology
+
+The [upstream collection](https://github.com/tradecatlabs/shulihuazixuecongshu) is an external reference provider. Its [rights statement](https://github.com/tradecatlabs/shulihuazixuecongshu#权利说明) does not grant a new license to the original prose, layout or scans. Titles were checked against the [catalog](https://github.com/tradecatlabs/shulihuazixuecongshu/blob/main/catalog.json) and book headings on **2026-10-05**:
+
+- 物理（第二册）: § 1.1 简谐振动; § 1.2 简谐振动方程; § 1.3 简谐振动方程中的参量; § 1.6 简谐振动的能量.
+- 平面解析几何, 第四章 圆锥曲线: § 4·5 椭圆的定义; § 4·6 椭圆的标准方程; § 4·7 椭圆的性质.
+
+`textbooks.ts` stores only source ID, collection/book/chapter/section labels, concept IDs, language, URL and `rightsStatus: "external-reference"`. The UI shows those labels, the **External textbook reference** marker and a link to the source book. It does not fetch or display book prose, scans or figures. Third-party content is not relicensed under this project's AGPL license. No textbook mapping is claimed for the linear-algebra lesson.
+
+`historicalAliases.json` contains four reviewed spellings: 倔强系数 / 倔強係數 → spring constant, and 振动的位相 / 振動的位相 → phase. The traditional spellings are explicitly marked as transcriptions in their source metadata. Both TypeScript and Rust extend their existing query lookup from this shared JSON; canonical names take precedence. Aliases do not become resource annotations or additional recall variants. The search context shows the legacy spelling alongside the modern resolved label. No bulk import is performed.
+
+## Security
+
+Definitions and equations are static reviewed source. Parameters and pointer input are bounded numbers. Scenes never accept expression strings, remote scripts, LLM-generated executable code or user HTML. JSXGraph labels use internal SVG text with parsing disabled. External resource and textbook URLs pass through the existing `httpUrl` and platform `openExternal` boundary.
+
+JSXGraph 1.13.3 is pinned. Its default entry includes an executable expression parser and a `Function`-based ES6 probe. The numeric-only module entry registers the required 2D primitives. The `jsxgraph-numeric-only` Vite plugin redirects JessieCode imports to `DisabledJessieCode`, whose expression entry points throw, and replaces the obsolete ES6 probe with a no-op because the application targets ES2021. It checks the exact probe before replacing it, failing on an unexpected upstream change. No installed dependency files are edited or vendored. Review this boundary when upgrading JSXGraph.
+
+KaTeX renders the authored equations as selectable HTML plus accessible MathML with `trust: false`, strict parsing and bounded expansion/size. There is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in lesson components. Browser regressions run the actual adapter with global eval and Function blocked and check that the application never attempts to use them; Playwright's own attempted string evaluation is separately identified by its UtilityScript stack. No remote executable script requests are allowed by that test.
+
+## Accessibility and localization
+
+All titles, explanations, invariants, parameter labels, presets and lesson UI messages have EN / zh-CN / zh-TW values. Numeric/math symbols are shared. Screen-reader users receive the step explanation, invariant, MathML, named controls and numeric readouts independently of the diagram. Changing steps announces the new reasoning. SVG has a descriptive accessible label. The panel focuses its heading, Escape returns to search, and closing restores focus to the initiating concept button. Existing search shortcuts do not act on hidden search results while the learning surface is open.
+
+Native buttons and range inputs support keyboard exploration, with visible focus. Force/velocity labels, numeric values and corner ordering complement color. `prefers-reduced-motion` disables playback while every meaningful static state remains accessible through steps/sliders. The diagram and explanation stack on narrow screens; the suite verifies a 390px viewport without horizontal overflow. The board itself is pointer-driven; keyboard manipulation uses equivalent labeled sliders.
+
+## Loading and performance
+
+The overview and compact path registry load with search. React.lazy imports `GuidedVisualization` only when a lesson or path entry is opened. Full lesson content, numeric scenes, JSXGraph, KaTeX, formula CSS/fonts and visualization CSS are in that dynamic dependency graph. Browser tests assert neither initial search nor the unopened overview requests lesson-engine assets. Search is independent of their successful loading; a lesson error boundary retains the overview and references.
+
+The three lessons currently share a single lazy engine chunk. This is deliberate for the small MVP; it is larger than 500kB uncompressed and produces Vite's chunk-size warning. Later modules can split by adapter/family as the registry grows. No Three.js, MathBox, physics engine, database, account or backend service is added. See the validation report for measured bundle sizes.
+
+## Validation and extension
+
+`npm test` includes `test:learning`: profile/visualization schemas, graph/path resolution, historical lookup, all localization fields, KaTeX equation parsing, state transitions, analytic SHM force/frequency/energy, ellipse distances/constraints, transformed basis/polygon area/orientation and numeric scene geometry. Existing assertions remain; the glossary assertion changes only to reflect the corrected SHM synonym. Search golden parity includes new lesson queries and legacy aliases.
+
+`test:web` and `test:web:build` both run the shared `visual_learning_regression.mjs` against real app assets. It covers search → overview → lesson, every step in every language, pointer dragging, keyboard sliders, play/pause/reset, all matrix presets, references, focus restoration, fallback, reduced motion, mobile layout and the security/lazy-loading boundaries. `test:desktop` also exercises native learning in the existing isolated test profile. Browser screenshots are generated under ignored `artifacts/visual-learning/`.
+
+To add a visualization:
+
+1. Reuse an ontology concept ID; add a canonical concept only if it is genuinely missing. Never use a second keyword matcher.
+2. Write the learning objectives, prerequisites and ordered path in `learning/registry.ts`. Every stage links to a real step.
+3. Author a `GuidedVisualizationDefinition` with all three languages. Each state must say what changes, what is invariant, why the next state follows and which equation describes it. Address a specific misconception in the explanation.
+4. Implement a pure numeric model and scene-family builder using the existing primitives. Extend the static scene union and renderer contract deliberately if new geometry is required; do not generate code at runtime.
+5. Add parameter normalization, mathematical invariant tests, localization/schema/path checks and actual browser interactions. Verify static reduced-motion states and a narrow viewport.
+6. Add only reviewed external metadata references, retaining their rights status. Keep any legacy recognition separate from canonical terms. Measure lazy loading and preserve all search/desktop regressions.
